## What £250 and £500 buy today {#hardware}

Examples from UK retailers' own pages on 19 November 2026, which will change before we ship:

• **About £250, a tablet:** the Lenovo Idea Tab, 11 inches, 8GB and 128GB, with a pen, £209.99 at John Lewis; or the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+, 11 inches, from £199 to £259 by option, also at John Lewis.

• **About £500, a tablet for AI on the device:** the Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 FE, 12GB and 256GB, with Galaxy AI, £509 at John Lewis. Two others to compare at the time, whose current prices we could not confirm: Lenovo's Yoga Tab, with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and 12GB, and the OnePlus Pad 3, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite and 12GB, launched at £529.

• **A European tablet:** the Volla Tablet, made by Volla in Germany, sold by Murena with /e/OS, a version of Android without Google: 12.6 inches, 12GB and 512GB, €569.99 in Murena's current offer, normally €649.99. Its chip is old and slow for AI on the device, but for sovereignty it is a strong choice: a European device and an open operating system.

• **Raspberry Pis:** a complete Raspberry Pi 5 starter kit, with the board, power supply, case with fan and a 64GB card, is £99.70 with 1GB of memory and £130.90 with 2GB at The Pi Hut. A static website needs very little memory, so about £250 buys two 2GB kits (£261.80), and about £500 buys five 1GB kits (£498.50) or three 2GB kits (£392.70); the backer chooses.

Memory prices have risen sharply this year, and Raspberry Pi prices with them, which is one more reason the promise is a spend, not a part list.

## What the hardware costs today {#hardware}

Examples from UK retailers on 19 November 2026, which will change before we ship:

• **Raspberry Pi, standard:** an iRasptek starter kit for the Raspberry Pi 5 with 8GB and a 128GB card, case, cooler and power supply, £229.99 on Amazon UK. At The Pi Hut, the official Pi 5 starter kit with 8GB is £224.50.

• **Raspberry Pi, Pro:** the same iRasptek kit with 16GB, £380.99 with a 128GB card and £397.99 with 256GB, on Amazon UK.

• **Tablet, about £250:** the Lenovo Idea Tab, 11 inches, 8GB and 128GB, with a pen, £209.99 at John Lewis; or the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+, from £199 to £259 by option, also at John Lewis.

• **Tablet, about £500:** the Samsung Galaxy Tab S10 FE, 12GB and 256GB, with Galaxy AI, £509 at John Lewis. Two others to compare at the time, whose current prices we could not confirm: Lenovo's Yoga Tab, with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and 12GB, and the OnePlus Pad 3, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite and 12GB, launched at £529.

• **A European tablet:** the Volla Tablet, made by Volla in Germany, sold by Murena with /e/OS, a version of Android without Google: 12.6 inches, 12GB and 512GB, €569.99 in Murena's current offer, normally €649.99. Its chip is old and slow for AI on the device, so it would be a European alternative at the Tablet Pro price without the local model: a sovereignty choice, not an AI one.

Memory prices have risen sharply this year, and Raspberry Pi prices with them, which is one more reason the devices are chosen at the time we buy them.

## Local AI on the Pro tiers, and sites made on the device {#on-device}

The difference between the standard and the Pro tiers is a local model. On the £400 Pi and the £500 tablet, we build the website for you with our own setup, and the device runs it; they could run a small model, but not well enough to be worth promising. On the £900 Pi Pro and the £1,000 Tablet Pro, the device runs a local model of its own. I have already tried a model running on my Web Summit tablet, in the browser; it was slow, but it worked, and for this it does not need to be fast. A Raspberry Pi 5 with 16GB should run useful open-weight models, more slowly; that is what we will test first.

That changes what the device is. It is not only where the site lives; it is where the site can be made. On the Pro tiers, point the build page from [watch your website being built](../../watch-your-website-being-built.md) at the device's own model, and a website is built on the device itself, with no key, no cloud and nothing leaving the house. The same model can run other tasks, and connect to other things the owner chooses. Some people will buy the appliance for that alone, because that is proper sovereignty: a computer they own, running a model they own, doing work for them under a behaviour policy they can read.

So the campaign should show it working: websites built entirely on a Pi Pro and on a Tablet Pro, published as examples, with how long each took.
